nodes.description: Tbx2 is expressed in non-chamber myocardium of the outflow tract and atrioventricular canal, where it represses chamber differentiation. Tbx2-null mice have atrioventricular canal patterning defects and defective outflow-tract septation, and Tbx2/Tbx3 compound mutants fail to form atrioventricular cushions, the precursors of valves and septa. These requirements match the conotruncal (double outlet right ventricle), septal, arterial-pole, and valvular defects reported in patients. Heterozygous null mice appear normal, so the patient defects imply that the human missense alleles fall below a dosage threshold the mouse heterozygote does not reach, or interact with other loci.

nodes.description: Patients have congenital vertebral segmentation and fusion defects (Klippel-Feil anomaly, thoracic fusions, hemivertebrae, rib fusions, and Sprengel deformity) with secondary scoliosis and kyphosis. TBX2 is expressed in developing bone and cartilage, but no model has shown how reduced TBX2 dosage disrupts somite segmentation or vertebral formation. This node records the human observation; its upstream link to TBX2 rests on the genotype-phenotype association.

nodes.description: In the mouse, Tbx2 and Tbx3 act redundantly upstream of Tbx1 and hedgehog ligand expression in pharyngeal endoderm, and loss of two of the three genes produces severe pharyngeal hypoplasia. The pharyngeal pouches give rise to the thymus and parathyroid glands, so reduced TBX2 dosage is proposed to produce the DiGeorge-like thymic and parathyroid deficits seen in patients. That the human thymic aplasia arises this way is an inference from the mouse network, not a direct observation.

nodes.description: Heterozygous missense variants p.Arg20Gln (N-terminal) and p.Arg305His (near the T-box) reduce TBX2 protein levels and its transcriptional repressor activity, and behave as partial loss-of-function (hypomorphic) alleles in Drosophila heterologous expression assays. The disorder is therefore attributed to reduced TBX2 dosage during embryonic development.
